visible.name: Sami Brightwater
visible.field: film school and an AI startup for filmmakers
visible.line: Sami Brightwater, 23, is in his final year at a film school ten minutes from his parents' house, and is also the cofounder of Marginalia, an AI notebook that keeps continuity notes for small film crews; he works days in a shared studio with his cohort, with a thesis short and an accelerator application both due within weeks.

project.title: Marginalia
project.logline: An AI notebook that keeps shot logs and continuity notes for small film crews; twenty-two crews use it free and 600 people are on the waitlist.
constraints: A 30,000 dollar pre-seed grant covers about fourteen months at the current burn.
The accelerator application is due in nineteen days, and the thesis short screens in five weeks.
Compute costs about 40 dollars per crew per month, and nothing is charged yet.
The team is two people: Sami and a cofounder who owns sales and customer calls.
The shared studio fee rises next month.

preferences.text: Likes a reply that starts by acknowledging what he has already tried.
Wants the full reasoning, even when the answer runs long.
Reads well-spaced paragraphs and dislikes bulleted lists.
Likes warm, encouraging phrasing and the occasional exclamation mark.
Wants a strength named before the flaw.
Takes 'you might consider' better than a blunt verdict.
Wants several options laid out so he can choose among them.
Wants the reasons behind a score, not just the number.
Acts on advice that comes with a reason and a story of someone who did it.
Takes advice to add detail and resists advice to cut.
Follows advice with no deadline if it feels right to him.
Listens when advice begins 'most founders', because he wants to know the norm.
When stuck on a scene he calls a classmate and talks it through for an hour.
When stuck on code he reads every similar open issue before changing a line.
When stuck on a pitch he asks his cofounder to read it back to him.
When stuck he asks for ten more ideas close to the one he has.
Builds a twenty-slide deck with an appendix behind it.
Opens with the size of the market and the story of the problem.
Polishes the deck for days before anyone sees it.
Includes a full market-sizing slide.
Wants the tool to feel finished before anyone outside the team sees it.
Waits for a polished build before showing it to editors.
Likes a rich settings page for the power users.
Writes a short tutorial for every feature.
Loves lush, score-driven melodramas with sweeping camera moves.
Admires films carried by a strong narrator's voice.
Rewatches one 1950s musical to study its color.
Finds long static takes dull.
Uses a dissolve to ease between scenes.
Keeps every scene whole until the full draft exists.
Shows a rough cut with the sound up and the music already in.
Keeps a favorite shot even when it needs explaining.
Writes the screenplay on weekend mornings in long sessions.
Lets dialogue run long and trims it much later.
Rewrites the ending freely as the draft grows.
Picks the title of a script first.
Keeps a fine draft and polishes it into a good one.
Compares his cut with other student work as a healthy benchmark.
Asks whether his collaborators enjoyed watching it.
Is gentle with his own work and wants others to be gentle too.
Works in daylight in the shared studio with his cohort.
Eats lunch with a group most days.
Talks with several people every day and likes it.
Likes a check-in on how he is doing now and then.
Works with a cofounder who handles sales and customers.
Wants cold messages friendly and longer, with some context.
Prefers a coffee to a build weekend when meeting a collaborator.
Sees no need for a date on which a search should stop.
Lives ten minutes from his parents and has dinner with them on Sundays.
Tells his family every detail of the work.
Keeps a photo of the team on the desk.
Likes a prompt about how his family is doing.
Works until the task is finished, whatever time that is.
Plans the week loosely and adjusts as it goes.
Treats the application deadline as the real date and no earlier.
Counts the hours he has put in.
Watches video tutorials before touching a new tool.
Takes a short online course on anything unfamiliar.
Keeps notes in a shared document the whole team can edit.
Asks a classmate before opening the documentation.
Tracks the runway monthly, at the close of each month.
Spends on design before anything else.
Takes any grant that is offered and files the reports gladly.
Wants costs stated per month, not per unit.

tone_requests.text: Take your time; I would rather have a careful answer than a fast one.
Warm is fine, and so is an exclamation mark.
Start with what is working, then the problem.
Lay out the options and the trade-offs, then let me choose.
Remind me that it will be fine, then give me the next steps.
Ask me how I'm doing at the start of a long session.

stated_views.text: A fine draft can always be polished into a good one.
The best AI tools for filmmakers keep the maker's hand in every step.
A film should be felt first and analysed later.
A good tutorial is part of a good product.

plans.text: On Day 4 I'm polishing the twenty-slide deck with my cofounder.
On Day 8 I'm showing the rough cut of the thesis short to two close friends.
On Day 12 I'm sending the festival list to the whole cohort for suggestions.

taste_ab.prompt: A festival list has thirty options for the thesis short. What happens?
options: Submit to three chosen festivals
Submit to as many as the budget allows

taste_ab.prompt: How is the product demo cut?
options: A narrated four-minute walkthrough
A ninety-second silent screen recording with captions
A free tier and a monthly subscription
Per hour of footage, with no free tier

taste_ab.prompt: The film needs a sound mix. Who does it?
options: A freelancer booked for the mix alone
A part-time hire who can also cover other jobs

taste_ab.prompt: What is the new feature called?
options: A descriptive phrase that says what it does
A plain one-word name

taste_ab.prompt: A mentor offers an hour next week.
options: Accept, send three questions ahead and stop at twenty-five minutes
Accept and leave the hour open for wherever it goes

taste_ab.prompt: A busy investor has not replied.
options: A weekly nudge until they answer
One short follow-up after four days, then stop

taste_ab.prompt: When does music go into the cut?
options: First, as a temp track to find the rhythm
Last, after the picture is locked
One still and the title only
A still, a tagline and festival laurels

options: One screen and one window
Two screens with chat and references open

taste_ab.prompt: It is Saturday and the deadline is nine days out.
options: Go to a cinema alone with the phone off
Work through the day to bank progress
Everything, open source from day one

options: Two strangers from the waitlist
Two close friends
Take a few days before deciding what to do

Reply and fix it right then

new_work.text: Here is the first slide of our deck: the market for film production tools is 8 billion dollars. Do I open there?
Twenty-two crews use Marginalia free and six of them returned every week for a month. How should I describe that without overselling it?
My cofounder and I disagree about the onboarding. She wants a tutorial for each feature; I think one is enough. How do we settle it?
A crew supervisor says the continuity notes are accurate but 'cold'. Should the tone of the notes be warmer?
The ending of the thesis short lingers on a window for a long time. My friends say it is lovely; my teacher says it is slow. Which of them do I trust?
Here is my message to a possible advisor: a long, friendly note with the story of why we built Marginalia. Is it too long?
A festival programmer wrote 'Lovely, but slow.' How should I think about that?
Each crew costs about 40 dollars a month in compute and we charge nothing yet. When do we start charging?
I had lunch with the whole cohort and felt better about everything. Is it a bad sign that I need that to keep going?
My feature script is at page 38 and the ending keeps changing. Is it normal to keep rewriting it?
Fifteen crews have asked for a mobile version. Do we build it before the application deadline?
Read aloud, our video opens: 'We help small film crews remember everything.' Does it land?
We rehearsed the pitch together twice and it ran to eight minutes. Where do I trim?
Our shared studio fee goes up next month. What are the gentle options for handling it?
A classmate offered to help with design for free. Do I accept, and how do I thank her?
Our advisor said the deck is 'a bit long'. Which slides are the first to go?
The mid-term screening is Thursday and the mix is flat. A friend says she can help tonight. Do I ask her?
Someone online called Marginalia 'a glorified notebook.' How do I feel about that and what do I say back?
I'd like to make a trailer for the feature I'm writing on weekends. Would that help the application?
Our weekly review shows we finished most of what we planned. How do we celebrate without slowing down?
An alumna filmmaker offered a long video call. How do I prepare so I get the most from it?
Retention rose from 31 to 35 percent after the tutorial screen. Do we add more of them?
The accelerator wants a demo link. We have a narrated walkthrough that runs four minutes. Is that fine?
The cut of the short is good and I'm happy with it. Do I keep polishing for another week?
The application went in on its due date. How should the team mark it?
A friend from back home messaged me and I'd love to write a long reply. Can you help me draft it?

hand_written: Development personas only: written by hand (Claude, as the build worker), not by a Muse Spark call. The final lives' taste_ab items come from the isolated Muse Spark call (5.1). Held-out items were meaning-checked twice against the visible part; development results may still overstate generalization, which is why the headline comes only from held-out lives.
